en: Liquid water expands by about nine percent in volume when it freezes into solid ice.
The troposphere, where most weather occurs, extends only about twelve kilometers above Earth's surface.
One liter of average ocean water contains about thirty-five grams of dissolved salts.
When five grams of iron completely rusts, it gains about two grams of mass by combining with oxygen.
Sound travels about four times faster in liquid water than it does through the air.
A single human hair is approximately one million carbon atoms wide.
Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, weighing about twice as much as lead for the same volume.
A single drop of human blood contains approximately five million red blood cells.
Solid carbon dioxide, called dry ice, sublimates directly into a gas at negative seventy-eight degrees Celsius.
Earth's atmosphere contains about twenty-one percent oxygen gas, which is necessary for combustion and rusting.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, liquefying only at three thousand four hundred twenty-two degrees Celsius.
At room temperature, one hundred milliliters of water can dissolve a maximum of thirty-six grams of table salt.
